title: Examples, Patterns & Context Design
description: Study choose representative examples, balance positive and boundary cases, organize long context, and avoid accidental instruction conflicts. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Choose representative examples
lessons.description: Add examples that break the spurious company-label correlation.
lessons.conceptOverview: Examples communicate mappings from inputs to outputs. Cover meaningful variations and edge cases, and avoid examples that contradict the written instruction or contain accidental shortcuts.
lessons.whyItMatters: Examples should teach the intended rule rather than accidental cues.

lessons.title: Balance positive and boundary cases
lessons.description: Add a partial invoice with an explicit missing-value output.
lessons.conceptOverview: Ordinary examples show successful behavior; boundary cases show when to abstain, reject or use an unknown value. Include both when the task has ambiguous inputs.
lessons.whyItMatters: Boundary examples clarify behavior when evidence is incomplete.

lessons.title: Organize long context
lessons.description: Create a context selection rule that preserves the exception and its source.
lessons.conceptOverview: Use document titles, identifiers and relevant excerpts to make evidence addressable. Evaluate placement effects and truncation instead of assuming every supplied detail receives equal attention.
lessons.whyItMatters: Context organization and budget affect evidence availability.

lessons.title: Avoid accidental instruction conflicts
lessons.description: Repair the conflict and add a parse-based check.
lessons.conceptOverview: Examples, templates and source text may contain competing directives. Keep trusted task instructions distinct and ensure examples demonstrate the same contract used for new inputs.
lessons.whyItMatters: Instructions and examples should agree on the output contract.
